title: Chloe, 29: The $400 Rent Upgrade

scenes.say: $14,400. That's what Chloe's nicer apartment costs over three years.
Her old place was $1,500 a month. The new one is $1,900.
$400 a month sounds small, until you multiply it.
Then add about $60 more for utilities and parking.
She earns about $66k, so $1,900 is roughly 35% of her gross pay.
The mistake wasn't the apartment. It was signing without the math.
Next lease: rent near 30%, count every fee, and sleep on it twice.
How much of your pay goes to rent? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because $400 more rent is $14,400 gone.

description: Chloe moved from a $1,500 apartment to a $1,900 one. That $400 a month is about $4,800 a year and $14,400 over three years, plus roughly $60 a month in extra utilities and parking. On a $66k salary her rent is now about 35% of gross pay. Numbers are rounded US estimates.
